patent.title: Method and apparatus for arithmetic coding and termination
patent.family_note: Package C SEP/patent-pool anchor. Via LA February 2026 AVC cross-reference chart lists US 6,825,782 claim 12 against H.264 §9.3 CABAC sections. NTT DOCOMO, INC. is a public AVC Patent Portfolio License licensor. Worldwide essential counterparts may exist in the Attachment 1 family; this ledger does not invent unlisted family members.

knowledge_origin.description: Public patent grant identifies Frank Jan Bossen inventorship and NTT Docomo, Inc. ownership of an arithmetic-coding / termination method and apparatus later mapped by Via LA into the AVC/H.264 essential-patent portfolio.

technology.problem: Efficiently encode/decode event sequences with arithmetic coding and correctly terminate / flush the bitstream so the decoder can reconstruct the same events.
technology.mechanism: Arithmetic encoder/decoder architecture with context sequencing, LPS probability estimation, range-register decoding, renormalization and termination/flush procedures for event sequences (CABAC-relevant entropy coding).
technology.comparison_baseline: Non-arithmetic / non-CABAC entropy coding alternatives for video bitstreams; arithmetic coding systems lacking the disclosed termination / flush control.

value_carriers.name: AVC/H.264 Patent Portfolio License (Via LA / formerly MPEG LA)
value_carriers.description: Public Via LA cross-reference chart includes US6825782 claim 12 in the AVC essential-patent portfolio mapping; NTT DOCOMO is a listed AVC licensor, enabling sublicenses under the multi-licensor portfolio license.

value_carriers.name: AVC / H.264 (ISO/IEC 14496-10 / ITU-T H.264) digital video coding standard
value_carriers.description: Pool administrator publishes an illustrative essential-claim map from US6825782 claim 12 to H.264 §9.3 CABAC sections after independent essentiality evaluation practice disclosed for the program.

value_carriers.name: AVC/H.264 compliant devices, software codecs and streaming/services ecosystem
value_carriers.description: A large public licensee roster shows program-level commercial uptake of the portfolio license across industries, but public sources reviewed do not map US6825782 individually to any named handset, OS codec, camera, STB or streaming implementation.

value_links.note: Confirms pool membership / licensor-mediated portfolio licensing rights transaction. Does not establish product implementation or single-patent royalty share.
Public pool chart maps claim 12 to H.264 §9.3 CABAC sections. This is SEP/standard essentiality evidence at the pool-evaluation level, not a court judgment and not a named-product claim chart.
Program-level licensee scale is public; exact US6825782 → named product implementation remains unknown.

gaps.description: Published AVC pool royalties and enterprise caps are program-level consideration. Via LA FAQ states royalties do not change with the number of essential patents. No public apportionment assigns any share of the pool rate card to US6825782.

gaps.description: V0.7 can record R2 for a single SEP inside a pool, plus standard essentiality evidence, but cannot represent the pool as a first-class network object: multi-licensor membership, rate-card independence from patent count, grant-back, licensee graph, essential-counterpart jurisdictions, or the difference between pool licensing and bilateral SEP cross-licenses.
needed_evidence: explicit pool vs bilateral licensing construct

notes: Package C SEP/patent-pool external replication. Standalone V0.7 analysis stops at R2 for US6825782 even though the surrounding AVC pool has a published worldwide rate card and a large licensee ecosystem. This is intentional: pool membership + licensor-mediated rights transaction are confirmed, but product implementation and patent-level attributable value must not be inherited from program-level royalties or licensee rosters. Complements the CRISPR portfolio case with a non-life-science, publicly listed patent-pool mechanism.
